That patch excerpt describes four behaviors:
- A new `darkbloom waitlist` command.
- Coordinator-gated approval for new sandbox setups (TB-013/T-061) and new cluster pairs.

- Fail-open behavior when the coordinator does not offer waitlists. The excerpt is truncated at "both new setups go on as in 0.".

All of this is documentation only; no source implementing waitlist gating was supplied. Gating sandbox setup behind a coordinator approval affects A-019/TB-013 only as an added precondition. The installer download and run-as-owner behavior is unchanged.

Open questions for integration:
- Whether the waitlist/approval client treats coordinator responses as untrusted and validates them.
- Whether the fail-open "coordinator does not offer waitlists" path can be forced by a network attacker. This would only skip an approval gate, not a security control, so its impact is availability or policy.
- Whether the TB-013 threat model text needs to mention the approval step.

No security regression is identifiable in the visible historical text. Missing source is a coverage limit.
